evidence.quote: |> List.choose (fun bookId -> Views.holdQueue bookId library |> Result.toOption)

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The three exports are Tier 3 projections built on existing view functions (Views.shelf, which uses Catalog.copiesAt and branch lookup; Views.holdQueue; Views.members). Whether a branch exists, which copies are shelved there and how holds queue up are all still decided by the existing Tier 1/2-backed code. The 'on loan until'/'on shelf' text only formats the existing DueBack projection and makes no new domain decision. The CLI only dispatches and renders views. No domain rule is decided in Tier 3/4.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The new exports write files only through the existing Files port and read state through the Store port. They add no direct System.IO use; the File.WriteAllLines in exportOverdue was already there. Nothing reads the clock, and nothing new touches Tier 1/2. The CLI calls only Tier 3 use cases.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Every fact the exports use (shelved copies, loan due dates, hold order, member type text) comes from the single existing projection or Tier 2 source. No limit, date rule or status derivation is copied. The member CSV format reuses the Views.members type rendering, which keeps it consistent with what import-members reads.

evidence.quote: let waitingFor bookId (library: Library) = queueFor bookId library |> List.length
| [ copyId; bookId ] -> Catalog.addCopy { Id = CopyId copyId; Book = BookId bookId; Branch = branch } library

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The holds-waiting count is defined in Tier 2 (Holds.waitingFor, built on queueFor), and Tier 3 only projects it. Import validation (unknown or duplicate copy, unknown book) is delegated to Tier 2's Catalog.addCopy, applied to the running library, so duplicates inside the file are caught by the same rule. The unknown-branch check goes through Catalog.findBranch. Tier 3 adds only CSV parsing (field count) and line numbering, which is input translation and not a domain rule. The 'HoldsWaiting > 0' guard in Reports only chooses the display text.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The import reads its file through the existing Files port and persists through the existing commit/Store path. An unreadable file becomes an explicit error value. No effect is added in Tier 1/2: Holds.waitingFor is pure. The CLI only dispatches to UseCases.importCopies and does not re-enter Tier 2. The JsonFileStore use in the backup branch was already there and is not changed.

evidence.quote: | None when entry.HoldsWaiting > 0 -> $"on shelf ({entry.HoldsWaiting} holds waiting)"

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The number of holds on a book has one definition, Holds.waitingFor, which reuses the existing queueFor; the view and the export both refer to it. The copy-adding rules are taken from Catalog.addCopy, not restated. No literal or predicate is copied across tiers.
